newsitem.title: UK: S&P starts new standard to classify mortgage loans.
newsitem.headline: S&P starts new standard to classify mortgage loans.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had introduced a new standard for classifying residential mortgage loans that relied on innovations in automated underwriting and mortgage scoring.

S&P said in a statement that automated underwriting and mortgage scoring allowed for greater objectivity in measuring risk associated with all mortgage transactions and could also lower borrower costs.
The seven risk grades, RG1 to RG7, replace the current A, B, C, and D loan designations.

Joint analysis by S&P and Freddie Mac of mortgage scoring during the past year strongly indicate the industry's need to change the standards and methods for evaluating and managing mortgage risk, S&P said.
S&P said the new standardised grading system was directly related to the foreclosure frequency.
"Through our joint efforts with S&P we're setting a standard for underwriting all mortgages," said Peter Maselli, Freddie Mac vice-president of automated underwriting.

"Our intensive research this past year has caused us to challenge the way loans have been underwritten and priced. We've peeled back the layers of risks associated with the entire mortgage market to redefine credit quality and refine credit risk evaluations in the process."
In preparing the study, S&P reviewed many of the top B and C lenders' guidelines, revealing inconsistent industry standards, S&P said.
